newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL BLUE-CHIP INDEX CLOSES UP, GAINS SEEN LIMITED.
newsitem.headline: KL BLUE-CHIP INDEX CLOSES UP, GAINS SEEN LIMITED.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed higher for the second day on Thursday, but analysts and fund managers said the upside was limited by lingering doubts over the direction of the local currency.
The benchmark Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed 9.71 points, or 1.07 percent, higher at 918.54, but off its intraday high of 921.16.
The ringgit's recent slide would continue to keep serious investors sidelined, said analysts.
"It all depends on whether the ringgit crashes," said a trader at the international division of a local brokerage.
The ringgit strengthened slightly against the U.S. dollar on Thursday, trading at 2.7620/70 at 1700 GMT, against 2.7810/30 at the close on Wednesday in Kuala Lumpur.
Key blue-chip issues were among the most actively-traded, including Telekom Malaysia Bhd and Sime Darby Bhd gaining 20 cents and five cents respectively.
Malayan Banking Bhd and power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd were also nibbled at by local and foreign institutions. The stocks gained 10 cents and 20 cents respectively.
Market volume stood at 237 million shares, valued at 1,357 million ringgit. Gainers outpaced losers 342 to 264.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot August contract gained 5.1 points to 918.5 with 1,026 lots traded. September futures gained 7.6 points to 922.0 with five lots having changed hands.
